messages.author: 615e5313dfc84fcc
messages.subject: Suggestions for file import
parts:
Hi All,

I will use R/qtl soon. I am planning to use data from a GBS study (genotyping by sequencing). We have ca. 50 F2 individuals and probably 5000 SNP markers. Before I start I would like to ask:

1) Is R/qtl appropriate to handle this data ? I will use it just because it is established in my lab.

2) Any suggestions on importing the data ? Can someone point me in the right direction to create suitable import files. What format do you vote is best to convert ? hmp ? vcf ? plain text ?

Many thanks for your attention to my question.

Sincerly,

Stefan

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Suggestions for file import
parts:
1. R/qtl should be able to handle the data, though some functions (e.g. plot.rf) don't work well with large numbers of markers.

2. I'd use "csv" or "csvr"; see http://www.rqtl.org/sampledata/

karl

messages.author: 615e5313dfc84fcc
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Suggestions for file import
parts:
Hi Karl,

Thanks a lot for your answer and your advise on this group. I actually found some threads dealing with GBS data, so it should be ok and I should read more before posting. However for the import format, maybe my phrasing was not clear. With the GBS data you usually go from the raw seq data through some kind of QC and variant calling pipeline. So you end up with a massive file containing actual nucleotides on chromosomal positions and heaps of other data that is irrelevant for R/qtl. I used TASSEL for this. TASSEL can generate VCF, hapmap, plain text other formats I dont understand yet. Going from these formats to an R/qtl readable file I will use the linux shell/awk and maybe some third-party tools (vcf-tools, PLINK?). My question was to the community: Are there any preferred ways to generate the csv or csvr files ? How do people handle allele recoding ?

Cheers,

Stefan
